intro.header: Hey there! You can call me Zach (it's easier that way)
intro.body: Great to meet you! I'm an agentic, Front-end leaning software engineer... but wait, what does that mean?
bullet-points: I love building apps using modern web-technologies (React, TypeScript, Vue)
While also building for things behind the scenes (Node, Next.js, Vite, Bun)
With AI being an accelerator in every stage (Cursor, OpenCode)
... And even running _inside_ the code itself! (LangChain Certified)

work-experience.description: Intellistack is like family to me - we worked on a lot of things together: from Salesforce Native form building, to the Streamline Data Fabric. I learned a lot here! This is called a "Data Fabric" - in other words, it's designed to be the middleman for your enterprise infrastructure and help you do cool workflows!
product-features: Search for a prospect in Salesforce, and file a progress report that's sent to internal staff through email or slack
Obtain a forecast posted via third-party webhook, and gather affected customers through an internal Database, issuing an automatically created report of stuff they're actively using.
Onboard an employee to the company using check-point based forms, that only pull up information based on who's viewing it.
Summarize a large chunk of processed information (via AI) to an outgoing third-party webhook, Google Drive, or Dropbox
personal-experience: Worked on Incoming and Outgoing webhooks, providing spaces to test a webhook with mock data
Constructed a Cards UI compatible with Material React Table's state. (Built from the ground-up!)
This helped customers use the data search comfortably on mobile devices
Built the version of the front-end components for Twilio, and Slack integrations
Re-structured Databricks telemetry for use across the Streamline monorepo
Became the documenter of MCP servers used throughout the engineering teams
Constructed agentic workflows for syncing Figma designs and Storybook components
Customized Microsoft's Monaco editor for use in workflow builders
Features a custom theme, syntax highlighting for Streamline's templates, drag-to-resize, and a header that shows the language being used

work-experience.description: This is a native forms builder on top of Salesforce! Here's what it's capable of:
product-features: Forms directly map to Salesforce Objects (Drag & drop!)
Launch, submit, and save forms for later
PCI-Compliant payments across several providers (Stripe, PayPal, Authorize, iATS)
Integrations with AWS, Dropbox, Azure, Formstack Documents and more
Wide selection of Pre-made themes (and custom ones too)
personal-experience: I was responsible for the Integration settings UI (https://help.formstack.com/hc/en-us/articles/44592554950547-File-Upload-Fields-with-Forms-for-Salesforce)

We built a payment field for the NativeCloud tier - it's written in React and auto-formats card number, CVV, and date (https://help.formstack.com/hc/en-us/articles/44593251541267-Stripe-Payments-Integration-Forms-for-Salesforce)

There is also an autosuggest field I helped build alongside the others - it can search, prefill, and obtain Salesforce records live (https://help.formstack.com/hc/en-us/articles/44592647592467-Lookup-Fields)

work-experience.description: This is a performance analytics dashboard, designed to review the specific inner-workings for the E3SM project. (And later other projects!) During this internship, this project was assembled from the ground up, utilizing Python, Flask, Bootstrap, MySQL, and Chart.js
personal-experience: Constructed the UI from the ground up, with the help of Bootstrap, and Chart.js
Built the main Python parsing utility for interpreting the analytics data
Data navigable through a custom tree hierarchy. Clicking on a data point on the chart helps to dive deeper into the specifics

questions.q: What food do you like to eat?!
questions.a: I love making pizza from scratch! Ones I love to make are the classic meat lovers, chicken spinach and alfredo pizza, and BBQ chicken + bacon.

questions.q: What editors do you enjoy using?
questions.a: I've recently been using Zed for most of my work, and that's despite being a hardcore VSCode user for 12 years! For all other things, vim is also a strong favorite.
Absolutely; I daily Arch on my personal laptop! Got a strong affinity for tiling window managers; started at i3, moved onto Sway, and most recently been exploring Hyprland.
